messages.subject: rank() function
parts:
Dear team, 
Thank you in advance for your time. 

I am trying to build a hierarchical model with random effects, and I am trying to do Posterior Predictive Checks (PPC) for my random effects (b0), in order to make this I have been using the following code:

 for( i in 1 : Subj ) {
    b0[i] ~ dnorm(0,tau)
    b0.rep[i] ~dnorm(0,tau)     
    rank.b0[i] <- rank( b0[1:Subj],i )
    rank.b0.rep[i] <- rank( b0.rep[1:Subj],i )
  }

Latter on the code the ranked() function in used in the following way: 
  # PPCs checking distribution of random intercept
  # Min and max of b0s
  tmin <- rank(b0[],1)
  tmax <- rank(b0[],Nsubj)
  tmin.rep <- rank(b0.rep[],1)
  tmax.rep <- rank(b0.rep[],Nsubj) 

This formulation is similar as it is implemented in BUGS, but for NIMBLE I am getting the following error:

defining model...
Error in getSymbolicParentNodesRecurse(code, constNames, indexNames, nimbleFunctionNames,  : 
  R function 'rank' has arguments that cannot be evaluated; either the function must be a nimbleFunction or values for the following inputs must be specified as constants in the model: b0[]

Is there any way to implement the rank() function, or am I missing something in the definition?

Thank you for your time.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: rank() function
parts:
Hi Diego,

Thanks for the question.  The rank function is not built in.  Some options would be to write it as a user-defined function (nimbleFunction -- see User Manual), to do posterior prediction as a post-processing step (unless you need to reduce the size of what is monitored for mcmc output, and the monitors2/thin2 doesn't help), or to use min and/or max if they can help you get what you want.  If you get stuck trying to write a user-defined function, please feel free to post another question saying how you want it to work (I think JAGS and WinBUGS have different rank functions, so it would be easiest if you say for sure what you want).

-Perry
